why: Rule 8: 16 candidates in 13 clusters, all sub-cm blips except two isolated short high-dQ/dx stubs, spread over 100 cm of z with no convergence and no readable direction, so I abstain rather than invent a reason.

The 291 cm cluster is a straight flat-MIP through-going track whose 9003 split is exactly collinear (trap 3), leaving only a fragmented 11 cm chain (38+101+39) 25 cm off it, all dQ/dx flat, so I take its upstream end on rule 2 alone.

Rule 1 plus rule 3: the 178 cm muon Bragg-rises to 220k at 19000 with a Michel-like blip 45014 8 cm away, so its cool free end 19001 is the vertex, and the 14 cm heavy prong starting 3.4 cm away at 19002 rises away at 88 degrees; rule 2 breaks the 19001/19002 tie.

Rule 1: the event is a single 62 cm track whose p4 profile is a textbook monotone stopping-muon Bragg rising to 310k at 10006, so the cool end 10000 is the only vertex candidate with its segment rising away.

11002 is a 172 degree collinear split (trap 3), while cluster 41's 6.4 cm MIP track is aligned to 11 degrees with the 11001-to-41007 gap vector and leaves 11001 at 89 degrees to the proton that Bragg-stops at 11000, making 11001 the real two-prong junction.
Rule 8: every cluster is at most 1.1 cm, and the only structure is a loose trail of blips with 17 cm of y spread over 93 cm of z, which shows no cone, no apex and no direction to read.

Rule 1 at full strength: 17004 is a 119 degree V apex in all three projections with 2 of 2 prongs rising away, one a 292 cm flat-MIP muon running downstream to z=500 and the other a 26.6 cm prong that Bragg-stops at 17011 with a 189k stub.

p4 resolves cluster 19's knot: two heavy prongs both leave 19004 cool at 70-75k and rise away to hot stops at 19003 and 19008, while the 39.6 cm prong's charge simply fades to 2k across the bridge from 19002, so 19004 is the true cool origin despite its 172 degree pair; the rival region is a spray with no apex.
Rule 1: 18002 is the only degree-2 vertex and both prongs rise away, one a monotone 67k-to-240k proton Bragg at 18000, but the prong pair opens 150.1 degrees so trap 3 costs it a tier.

A four-prong heavily-ionising proton star with the charge peaking at 20006 (288-395k) and prongs Bragg-stopping at 20003 and 20002, and the 67.6 cm flat-MIP track back-extrapolates to within 1.1 cm of 20006 versus 2.1 cm of 20054.

29019 is the only junction in the event, a degree-3 apex opening 107 degrees at the lowest z (122.6) with both prongs running forward in z: a 61.7 cm flat-MIP muon exiting the top corner and a 34.1 cm 2x-MIP prong downstream.

Rule 1 makes 6000 the cool start of a textbook 55 cm stopping muon (flat 55k rising on the template to 128k at 6001), but it sits on the cathode and is single-prong, and the seven unmeasured blips 140 cm away in y are a real alternative I cannot read.

The 1.7 cm stub 21002-21003 is collinear to 8 degrees with the 9001-to-21002 gap vector in all three projections, so it is one broken prong leaving 9001 at 72 degrees from the 224k proton stub, and 9001 is also the lowest z.

19002 is the only junction, a 94 degree V carrying a large vertex charge blob on both prongs (245k and 168k over the last 2 cm, then 55-60k beyond), with the 46 cm prong running forward in z and Bragg-stopping at 19000.

Rule 1 at full strength: a degree-3 vertex with 3 of 3 prongs rising away, each with a p4-confirmed monotone template Bragg - a 99 cm muon stopping at 19000 and 29.7 cm and 15.2 cm protons stopping at 19001 and 19003.
